==English==
{{wp}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|pô|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/pɔː(ɹ)/}}
* {{enPR|pôr|a=GenAm}}, {{IPA|en|/poɹ/}}
* {{enPR|pōr|a=rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}}, {{IPA|en|/po(ː)ɹ/}}
* {{IPA|en|/poə/|a=non-rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-pore.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|pour|;|poor<aa:pour-poor>|;|paw<aa:non-rhotic,horse-hoarse>}}

===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=skin opening|:inh|enm:pore<ety:bor<fro:pore>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|pore}}, from {{der|en|fro|pore}}, from {{der|en|la|porus|id=pore}}, from {{der|en|grc|πόρος|t=passage}}. Displaced native {{ncog|en|sweat hole}} from {{ncog|enm|swet hole}}, which might have been a reformation of {{ncog|ang|swātþȳrel|lit=sweat hole}}, which competed with {{m|ang|līcþēote|lit=body pipe}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# A [[tiny]] [[opening]] in the [[skin]].
#: {{syn|en|sweat hole}}
#: {{ux|en|I could sense the sweat dripping out of all my '''pores'''.}}
# By extension any small opening or [[interstice]], especially one of many, or one allowing the passage of a [[fluid]].
#: {{ux|en|the '''pores''' of a rock.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=[[w:Walter Johnson (academic)|Walter Johnson]]|chapter=The Rebirth of the Progressive Movement|title={{w|William Allen White}}’s America|location=New York, N.Y.|publisher=w:Henry Holt and Company|year=1947|section=part IV (Normalcy and Reform)|page=436|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/williamallenwhit00john/page/436/mode/1up|oclc=377736|passage=After reading White’s vitriolic language, ''{{w|The New York Times}}'' facetiously remarked that “Kansas is bleeding from every '''pore''' of her vocabularium. Sharp’s rifles are discharging from the well-known Emporium of White & Son, unlimited, and Bibles are closed until after election.”}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{der|en|enm|poren}}, {{m|enm|pouren}}, {{m|enm|puren|t=to gaze intently, look closely}}, from {{der|en|ang|*pūrian}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*pūrōn}}, suggested by {{cog|ang|spyrian|t=to investigate, examine}}. Akin to {{cog|stq|puurje|t=to question, investigate; pry, prod}}, {{cog|fy|poarje|t=to poke, prod}}, {{cog|dum|poren|t=to pore, look}}, {{cog|nl|porren|t=to poke, prod, stir, encourage, endeavour, attempt}}, {{cog|nds|purren|t=to poke, stir}}, {{cog|da|purre|t=to poke, stir, rouse}}, dialectal {{cog|sv|pora}}, {{m|sv|pura}}, {{m|sv|påra|t=to work slowly and gradually, work deliberately}}, {{cog|ang|spor|t=track, trace, vestige}}. Compare also {{cog|enm|puren}}, {{m|enm|piren|t=to look, peer}}. See {{l|en|peer}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# To [[study]] [[meticulous]]ly; to go over again and again.
#* {{RQ:Mary Shelley Last Man|I|10|passage=Yet each foreign post day she watched for the arrival of letters - knew the postmark, and watched me as I read. I found her often '''poring''' over the articles of Greek intelligence in the newspaper.}}
# To [[meditate]] or [[reflect]] in a steady way.
